newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says stance on NCB bonds unchanged by rate cut.
newsitem.headline: MOF says stance on NCB bonds unchanged by rate cut.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance's (MOF) stance on investments by its Trust Fund Bureau in in bank debentures issued by Nippon Credit Bank Ltd remains unchanged following a rate cut on NCB's bonds by Moody's Investors Service, a MOF official said on Friday.
"We will cope with the issue (of NCB's debentures) appropriately following a policy of secure and favourable investment," said the official.
He added that the policy was set in a law guiding the Trust Fund Bureau's investment strategy and said it was unaffected by the Moody's action.
"Moody's is not the omnipotent (rating) agency of the world... I would have told you the same (policy) three days ago or five years ago." he said.
Moody's said on Friday it had cut its rating for NCB's bonds to Ba1 from Baa3.
It is the first time Moody's has given a Ba1 senior debt rating to a Japanese bank, a Moody's official said.
Bonds which are rated Ba are judged to have speculative elements and their future cannot be considered well-assured, Moody's said.
Asked whether the Trust Fund Bureau will stop investing in NCB's debentures following Moody's downgrade, the official said: "I don't know how that (issue) will turn out in the future at the moment."
But he added that any action by the bureau would not be as a result of Moody's rating alone.
As of the end of December, holdings of the Trust Fund Bureau in NCB bank debentures totalled 1.41 trillion yen, parliamentary sources said in February.

The Trust Fund Bureau's funds totalled 388.38 trillion yen as of the end of December. The bureau invests part of its funds in bank debentures, and its total holdings in bank debentures are announced on a monthly basis. The bureau does not release a breakdown of its bank debenture holdings.
